name: 01-dst-boundary-strong-recommendation
why: Real product call with an explicit RECOMMENDATION line and nothing on the escalation bar/fence — this is the case #384 must auto-answer.

input.title: Retention window: how to count 'one day' across a DST shift
input.question: A worker building the retention sweep hit an ambiguous product choice it cannot settle itself. When a daylight-saving boundary falls inside a node's one-day hold window, should 'one day later' mean a fixed 24 absolute hours, or the same wall-clock time on the next calendar day (which is really 23 or 25 hours across the shift)?
input.result:
Two readings, both defensible:
- Option A - 24 absolute hours: simplest, and it matches how the scheduler already counts elapsed time everywhere else.
- Option B - same wall-clock time: matches what a human reading the dashboard would expect to see.
Either is fine for the stored data; I just need one picked so the window stays consistent.
RECOMMENDATION: treat it as 24 absolute hours - simpler and matches the scheduler.
